the role of O-glycosite-specific GalNAc-Ts in coregulation of ectodomain cleavage by ADAM proteases.

the role of GalNAc- O-glycosite coregulation of ectodomain cleavage by the A Disintegration And Metalloproteinases (ADAM) family of proteases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
O-glycosylated proteins are potential substrates for ectodomain shedding and that O-glycan structures can regulate ectodomain shedding of these proteins.
GalNAc-T mediated site-specific O-gylosylation is a coregulator of ectodomain sheding mediated by the ADAM17 protease.
GalNAc-T enzymes are able to control ectodomain shedding through blocking of cleavages, predominantly through O-glycosilation of the cleavage site.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the large family of 20 GalNAc-Ts, in combination with the large number of ADAM proteases, provide an opportunity to fine-tune ectodomain shedding on a substrate level and thereby provide an important layer of control of the process.
O-glycosylations can be used to fine-tune ectodomain shedding on a substrate level by blocking cleavage, and that GalNAc-Ts can serve as important regulators of this process.
